S1 — BLOCKING: turn-transaction-v1 falsely guarantees rollback for any tool error.
Violated invariant/authority: eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12 DESIGN D1/D2 and acceptance criteria require each selected capability to state its actual operation, limits and residual interpretation truthfully; ADR 0020 section 3 makes atomic state mutation/rollback a bounded positive commitment. Effective profile: semantic-system within rules-clause-complete.
File:line: packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityInventory.ts:2491. It says any failure, specifically a model or tool error, rolls back every turn write and leaves only a post-rollback diagnostic.
Concrete scenario: Run a normal unaudited turn for a PC at 15 HP; the model successfully calls adjust_hp with amount -2, then supplies invalid adjust_hp arguments, then returns nonempty narration within the round budget. The failed call is returned to the model, the turn is accepted, HP 13 and the accepted trace persist. ToolRegistry.invoke returns invalid_args/unknown_tool and wraps a thrown tool exception as tool_error rather than throwing (toolRegistry.ts:226-243). runToolLoop records these results and continues (turnLoop.ts:311-377). runTurn with no auditor releases the candidate savepoint without rejecting failed results (orchestrator.ts:1058-1078), and an auditor can also explicitly accept such a candidate (1101-1102). The outer rollback catches escaping failures, not every ToolResult with ok:false. Existing orchestrator.test.ts:501-539 expressly accepts malformed arguments through the recoverable path; :725-749 records an accepted trace/quality flag after a failed call.
Ownership/consumer/consequence: The PR's authoritative internal inventory and accepted ownership finding are the affected consumers. This statement promises a stronger state-integrity boundary than the selected runtime provides; a caller/reviewer relying on it would incorrectly infer successful writes were undone merely because another tool failed. This is a metadata/contract defect in the current PR, not a demand to change established turn behavior.
Sibling analysis: Examined unknown_tool, invalid_args, parsed request failure, returned domain errors and caught tool exceptions; successful writes before/after the failure; no auditor, ordinary auditor acceptance, rejection/retry and presentation-only repair. Recoverable result failures do not inherently abort. Escaping model/orchestration exceptions, exhausted tool rounds, empty narration and terminal audit rejection do abort; rejected candidate savepoints are separately rolled back. The presentation-only repair branch's prohibition on failed calls must not be generalized to ordinary acceptance.
Required closure/next state: State the actual distinction between recoverable failed tool results and failures that escape/abort the turn, and the separate candidate rejection boundary. Reconcile the whole turn/audit/error family and its citations instead of changing runtime to satisfy this prose. Review registry ownership reasoning for consistency after the correction.
Permanent evidence: GENERALIZED INVARIANT, proportionately using the existing recoverable-tool-error, accepted-trace and turn/candidate rollback tests together with the actual dispatch/acceptance code. No new per-error behavioral suite or prose/AST semantic checker is required for this inventory correction.
Repair material: YES; it narrows an authoritative atomicity guarantee.

S2 — BLOCKING: the spell-duration statements generalize guards across supported source forms and different lifecycle operations.
Violated invariant/authority: eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12 DESIGN D1/D2 and acceptance criteria require truthful operation/exclusion boundaries grounded in the real engine; ADR 0020 section 3 requires positive bounded commitments. SRD 5.1 p.143 and the vendored records for Find Familiar and Find Steed establish that instantaneous casting can create a persistent bond. Effective profile: semantic-system within rules-clause-complete.
File:line: packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityInventory.ts:472 (start_effect) and :559 (refresh_effect).
Concrete scenario A: start_effect with kind summoning, source spell:find-familiar (or spell:find-steed), a durable caster and one linked actor, duration until-removed succeeds and creates the persistent bond. The operation instead says instantaneous spells are refused and a parseable record duration must match. activeEffects.ts:3589-3600 explicitly admits an instantaneous spell whose mechanics supply a persistent-linked summoning effect; :3628-3668 enforces the bond-specific duration/caster/topology. bondedSummonTransitions.test.ts:71-83 uses the real start_effect tool for both spells. Their records and the vendored PDF p.143 say Instantaneous. The later bonded-summon exclusion does not explicitly qualify the operation's categorical refusal/duration-match claim.
Concrete sibling B: Start a valid spell-effect for spell:continual-flame with duration until-removed, then refresh_effect with duration {kind:'timed',amount:1,unit:'hour',anchor:'spell-cast'}. The declared duration passes validateDuration; refreshEffect changes it and records the refreshed event. The inventory instead promises every parseable spell duration must be kept. activeEffects.ts:6216-6245 checks record equality only for parsed.kind === 'timed' when a replacement duration is supplied; it does not impose the create-time until-dispelled or until-dispelled-or-triggered grounding. Continual Flame is Until dispelled (records.json and vendored PDF p.130); Glyph of Warding supplies the until-dispelled-or-triggered sibling (pp.149-150). Existing activeEffects.test.ts:473-500 shows their create-time refusal boundaries; :2032-2099 protects timed refresh and active/suppressed/ended status, not a universal refresh guard.
Ownership/consumer/consequence: These new authoritative tool capability statements incorrectly deny a supported source-backed bond and overstate refresh duration fidelity. They obscure the actual execution/adjudication boundary. The existing refresh tool description repeats the broader assertion, but engine behavior remains the truthfulness criterion; copying that description cannot authorize the inventory claim. This finding does not itself authorize a new runtime mechanic.
Sibling analysis: Examined instantaneous ordinary spells versus persistent-linked summons; timed, until-dispelled, until-dispelled-or-triggered and unparsed source durations; source ref resolution and ruling/item sources; create versus refresh; supplied versus omitted replacement duration; active/suppressed/ended; concentration/profile requirements and durable caster/topology constraints. Timed amount/unit equality is real; the persistent bond exception is real; the non-timed create guards are not universal refresh guards. Treat both sites as one duration-boundary statement class, not two isolated wording examples.
Required closure/next state: Explicitly state the persistent-linked summon exception and describe refresh's actual duration validation scope, including the limits of spell-record grounding. Reconcile the whole effect duration/source/lifecycle family against the executable branches, not a paraphrased tool description. Preserve residual DM interpretation and disclose limits without inventing an engine repair in this inventory-only PR.
Permanent evidence: GENERALIZED INVARIANT for the duration-form/call-boundary distinctions, using the existing create/refresh/status evidence and branch inspection. RETAIN the existing EXACT SOURCE-BACKED Find Familiar/Find Steed bond evidence and ordinary-instantaneous refusal evidence; no new permanent near-duplicate reproducer or symbol/prose census is required. No source-fidelity assertion is weakened or replaced.
Repair material: YES; it changes the authoritative supported/refused source and duration boundaries.
